subject: Randomized Response Technique analysis with Structural Equation Modeling in R

messages.author: 2ba069d5a92c202d
messages.subject: Randomized Response Technique analysis with Structural Equation Modeling in R
parts:
Dear all,

I'm analyzing some data I gathered about sensitive behavior with Randomized Response Technique (RRT). The majority of packages to deal with RRT in R adopts modified logistic regressions to treat the response variable, while I would be more interested in fitting a Structural Equation Model (SEM) to model the effect of several drivers on reported behavior.
I found that some authors found a way to model RRT with SEM on the software Mplus (Hox, J., & Lensvelt-Mulders, G. (2004). Randomized response analysis in Mplus. Structural equation modeling, 11(4), 615-620.). 
However, I am a satisfied R user and I love the 'lavaan' and 'blavaan' package for latent variable analysis. Would you suggest me a way to fit a SEM on the RRT response with 'lavaan'?

Yours sincerely,

Jacopo Cerri

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Randomized Response Technique analysis with Structural Equation Modeling in R
parts: Would you suggest me a way to fit a SEM on the RRT response with 'lavaan'?

Mplus can fit mixture models (read the Mplus syntax in the Appendix of that article), whereas lavaan cannot.  The nlsem package can fit mixture models, but I couldn't say whether you would be able to fit the RRT with it.  You could certainly fit a mixture with a Bayesian program (BUGS, JAGS, Stan), but you'll probably have to figure out how to program it on your own rather than use blavaan.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
